editorial.title: Who Is Vishal Sikka? The AI Pioneer Who Ran Infosys — and Just Raised $85 Million to Disrupt It
editorial.excerpt: Nine years after a bruising exit from Infosys, the 59-year-old former SAP CTO has founded Hang Ten Systems, an enterprise AI startup that closed $85 million in seed funding in four months — with Intel and Micron's CEOs writing checks.
editorial.image_caption: Vishal Sikka speaking at SAP's SAPPHIRE conference in Orlando in 2010, when he was the company's first-ever CTO. In 2026 he founded Hang Ten Systems, an enterprise AI startup that has raised $85 million in seed funding.
editorial.nri_angle: Sikka's arc — small-town Madhya Pradesh to Stanford mentorship under AI's founding fathers to the top of Infosys and SAP, and now a founder again at 59 — embodies the Indian diaspora's outsize role in the AI era.

just_in.title: Diwali Gifting Gets Pricier: Pistachio, Almond Prices Surge Ahead of Festival
just_in.excerpt: Pistachio prices are up 30–40% and almonds 10–20% as the US-Iran conflict disrupts Iranian supplies, freight rates climb, and a weak rupee inflates import costs — with traders expecting festive sales to fall 10–15%.
just_in.image_caption: Pistachios at a dry-fruit market. Pistachio prices in India have risen 30–40 percent year-on-year ahead of Diwali on supply disruptions and higher freight costs.
just_in.nri_angle: NRIs sending Diwali hampers to India face the same 15–30% inflation, though almonds bought at the Californian origin may be relatively cheaper than Indian retail.

just_in.title: September's Global Immigration Shifts: What Changed for Visa Seekers Worldwide
just_in.excerpt: From Australia's new skilled-visa priority rules to Japan's twentyfold permanent residence fee hike and a UK settlement overhaul on the horizon, September brought rule changes that directly affect Indian migrants.
just_in.image_caption: WR Immigration's September 2026 global immigration recap graphic. The recap covers rule changes in Canada, Australia, the United Kingdom, Japan, Saudi Arabia, New Zealand, and Thailand.
just_in.nri_angle: Australia's onshore-first processing favors Indian students and graduates already in the country, while the UK's coming earned-settlement overhaul could reshape ILR eligibility for thousands of Indians nearing five years of residence.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Rahul Gandhi Accuses Delhi Police of Silencing Women Over Harassment Complaints
just_in.excerpt: The Leader of Opposition said women protesters and journalists faced mistreatment by Delhi Police during October 3 demonstrations at Jantar Mantar, and demanded CCTV footage from Saket police station be made public.
just_in.image_caption: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi meets journalists Shaheen Khan and Nafisa Khan, who alleged assault at Saket police station. Gandhi posted a video of this interaction alongside his attack on Delhi Police over the handling of sexual harassment complaints.
just_in.nri_angle: Overseas Indians follow Indian political developments closely; the standoff adds another flashpoint to the SIR controversy and the broader debate over policing of protests and press freedom in the world's largest democracy.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Pune Lab's HPV Self-Sampling Kit Aims to Expand Cervical Cancer Screening
just_in.excerpt: Greenarray Labs has launched CerviSens, a vaginal self-sampling kit for high-risk HPV testing that skips the speculum exam. A 203-sample validation study reported 98.0% sensitivity and 99.4% specificity versus clinician collection.
just_in.image_caption: Greenarray Labs representatives at the launch of CerviSens, the company’s HPV self-sampling kit, in Pune. The kit allows women to collect their own vaginal sample for high-risk HPV testing without a speculum examination.
just_in.nri_angle: Many NRI families arrange health checkups for relatives in India; a validated self-sampling option is worth flagging to women back home who have skipped cervical screening, and India's screening gap is a known concern in diaspora health philanthropy.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: US Marine Arrested After Strangling Death of Japanese Woman in Okinawa
just_in.excerpt: Lance Corporal Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, was arrested on suspicion of murder and robbery after Anna Yagi, 39, was found dead in a Naha hotel room. Japan's prime minister lodged a formal protest and demanded full US cooperation.
just_in.nri_angle: The case will be watched in New Delhi, where India's deepening defence ties with the United States and Japan run through the Quad — and where past Okinawa incidents have fed public debate about the costs host communities pay for foreign military presence.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Two Killed, Indian Seafarer Injured as Russian Drone Sinks Turkish Cargo Ship
just_in.excerpt: A Russian drone strike set fire to the Turkish-owned cargo vessel Royad Mammadov in the Black Sea, killing the captain and one other crew member. Three Indian nationals were aboard; one was injured and is receiving treatment in Romania.
just_in.nri_angle: India supplies a large share of the world's merchant seafarers, and Indian crew routinely serve aboard foreign-flagged cargo ships transiting the Black Sea — putting Indian nationals directly in the line of fire as drone attacks on civilian shipping escalate.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: OpenAI to Add Invisible Text Watermarks to ChatGPT and Codex in the EU
just_in.excerpt: OpenAI's textGrain system subtly shapes word choices so detectors can spot AI-generated text, complying with the EU AI Act. API developers worldwide can opt in; the detector stays limited to approved researchers.
just_in.image_caption: The ChatGPT app icon on a smartphone. OpenAI said it will add an invisible statistical watermark to eligible ChatGPT and Codex text in the European Union over the coming weeks.
just_in.nri_angle: No change for users outside the EU — watermarking is EU-only and opt-in on the API — but educators, employers and compliance teams should know these marks are invisible, fragile and often absent.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Schneider Electric to Buy PTC for $22.6 Billion in Its Biggest Deal Ever
just_in.excerpt: The $205-a-share all-cash offer, a 42.3% premium, sent PTC shares up nearly 34% on Monday. Schneider's stock fell about 10% in Paris as investors weighed the price and the up-to-EUR-23-billion financing plan.
just_in.image_caption: Schneider Electric’s headquarters. The French engineering group agreed to acquire US industrial software company PTC for $22.6 billion in cash.
just_in.nri_angle: No direct impact for most readers, but the deal is another major bet on data-centre and industrial-AI infrastructure, a sector employing a large Indian tech workforce in the US and Europe.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Mom's Biryani Brings Homestyle Dum Biryani to Sunnyvale's Crowded Indian Food Lane
just_in.excerpt: The Fremont Avenue restaurant calls itself Sunnyvale's top pick for authentic Indian food — a claim born from its own press release, but diners give it a solid 4.6 out of 5.
just_in.image_caption: The Mom's Biryani storefront at 103 East Fremont Avenue in Sunnyvale. The homestyle restaurant holds a 4.6-out-of-5 rating across nearly 400 reviews.
just_in.nri_angle: For Bay Area Indians, homestyle spots like Mom's Biryani are everyday infrastructure — the taste of home for tech workers and the go-to for family dinners and celebrations.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Keerthy Suresh's Dorothy Crosses ₹10 Crore, Tamil Cinema's 10th Hit of 2026
just_in.excerpt: The Karthik Subbaraj period drama bounced back on its second weekend to cross the success threshold, turning steady word-of-mouth into a rare mid-budget box-office win.
just_in.image_caption: Actress Keerthy Suresh. Her period drama Dorothy crossed Rs 10 crore at the Indian box office in its second week, becoming Tamil cinema's 10th successful venture of 2026.
just_in.nri_angle: Dorothy crossed $180,000 in North America in week one with expanded week-two screenings — a festival-premiered Tamil film that diaspora audiences are keeping alive on big screens.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: With Asian Games Gold Secured, India Hockey Eyes Los Angeles 2028
just_in.excerpt: India's men defended their Asian Games hockey title with a 5-1 win over Malaysia, the women ended a 44-year wait against China, and both squads have booked direct tickets to LA 2028.
just_in.image_caption: India's men's hockey team celebrates with gold medals behind an LA 2028 'Qualified' banner. The 5-1 win over Malaysia in the Asian Games final was India's first successful title defence and booked a direct Olympic berth.
just_in.nri_angle: LA 2028 lets Indian-Americans watch India chase Olympic hockey gold on home soil for the first time, with both the men's and women's teams qualified directly.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Archery Premier League Returns to Hyderabad as Asian Games Stars Turn Rivals
just_in.excerpt: Less than a week after India won nine Asian Games archery medals, the stars trade national jerseys for franchise rivalries in the Archery Premier League's second season, running October 8–18 in Hyderabad.
just_in.image_caption: The Archery Premier League logo. Season 2 of the franchise archery league begins in Hyderabad on October 8, with 48 archers across six teams competing over 11 days.
just_in.nri_angle: The APL gives Indian fans abroad a new way to follow archery — and an early look at the archers India will field at Los Angeles 2028, which many in the US diaspora will attend.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: BJP drops Hardeep Puri, Smriti Irani in fresh UP Rajya Sabha slate of 8
just_in.excerpt: The BJP announced an entirely new slate for the October 16 biennial elections to ten Rajya Sabha seats from Uttar Pradesh, with no sitting member renominated and two Union ministers left out.
just_in.image_caption: Hardeep Singh Puri, former Union minister. (Wikimedia Commons)
just_in.nri_angle: Uttar Pradesh's Rajya Sabha bloc shapes legislation touching the diaspora — emigration, citizenship and fiscal bills — and Puri's exclusion raises the question of who holds the petroleum portfolio, with direct relevance to energy prices.

just_in.title: Thailand floods kill 31 as forecast warns of more rain and flash flooding this week
just_in.excerpt: The Interior Ministry confirmed 31 deaths from flooding since September 16, as meteorologists forecast thunderstorms and heavy rain across upper Thailand through Wednesday.
just_in.image_caption: Floodwaters in Hat Yai, Songkhla province, during Thailand's 2010 floods — file photo. (Wikimedia Commons)
just_in.nri_angle: Thailand is a top destination for Indian travellers and home to a large Indian expatriate community; with Diwali season nearing, travellers should allow extra transit time and keep plans flexible as floods disrupt roads while airports and city rail keep running.

news.title: Three Doctors Turn Delhi–Aizawl Flight Into a Flying Emergency Ward
news.excerpt: A passenger with chronic kidney disease suffered severe oxygen desaturation mid-flight — and three doctors travelling on board improvised a ward in the cabin until the plane landed in Aizawl.
news.image_caption: An Air India aircraft; the Delhi–Aizawl flight where three doctors attended to a passenger's mid-air medical emergency
news.nri_angle: For the diaspora flying long-haul to India with elderly parents or chronic conditions, this rescue is a reminder to keep medical records and prescriptions in cabin baggage and brief the cabin crew on boarding.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Jaishankar Calls US a 'Lonelier Power', Urges Middle Path Between America and China
news.excerpt: At the Munich Leaders Meeting, the external affairs minister said Washington had deliberately drifted, China is rising sharply, and middle powers must navigate between them with a 'Goldilocks' balance.
news.image_caption: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, who described the US as a 'lonelier power' at the Munich Leaders Meeting
news.nri_angle: For the diaspora, this is the clearest articulation of the foreign-policy weather they live in: Jaishankar's balancing act between a repositioning America and an assertive China will shape the trade, technology and immigration policies that touch Indians abroad.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: IRDAI's Insurance Commission Overhaul Sparks Fears for One Million Brokers' Jobs
news.excerpt: The regulator wants to cap commissions and cut insurers' expense limits by a third; brokers say the maths will kill jobs and leave small-town customers unserved.
news.image_caption: A blue keyboard key labelled "insurance" with an umbrella icon on a white keyboard. IRDAI has proposed caps on insurance commissions and a one-third cut in insurers' expense limits, sparking a fight with the brokers' industry body over jobs.
news.nri_angle: For NRIs holding Indian life and health policies, the fight is worth watching: leaner distribution economics could mean cheaper premiums and cleaner sales practices, or thinner broker networks in smaller towns where insurance penetration is lowest.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Ukraine's Robot Offensive Reclaims Donetsk Villages as Winter Approaches
news.excerpt: Explosives-packed BTR-60s driven by remote control helped Ukraine retake villages in Donetsk, while an ex-minister's new "Army of Robots" project promises to mechanise the war's deadliest jobs.
news.nri_angle: For the Indian diaspora, the operation is a gauge of the war's trajectory: India's balanced posture on the conflict, the war's drag on energy and food prices, and the safety of remaining Indian nationals in Ukraine all turn on how long the fighting lasts.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Flydubai Hijack Suspect Likely Acted Alone, Investigators Say, as Australia Link Emerges
news.excerpt: Israeli officials say early evidence points to a lone attacker with no established group or state backing, while Australian agencies examine the Omani co-pilot's 2015-2017 residence on a student visa.
news.image_caption: A flydubai Boeing 737 in flight. Flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv was targeted in an attempted hijacking on September 30, with 174 passengers aboard.
news.nri_angle: The flight's captain, Smit Machchhar, is of Indian origin and was hailed as a hero for saving 174 passengers — a point of pride and attention for Indian travelers on Gulf routes.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Right to Vote in 'Great Peril,' Justice Nariman Warns as Executive Grip Tightens
news.excerpt: In a September 27 oration, the former Supreme Court judge cited 90 lakh exclusions in West Bengal's voter-roll revision and called the executive's grip on Election Commissioner appointments a "red flag."
news.image_caption: Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman, former Supreme Court judge of India, who warned that the right to vote is in 'great peril'
news.nri_angle: India's standing as the world's largest democracy rests on credible elections; NRIs who defend that record abroad have the most to lose when a former Supreme Court judge says the right to vote is in peril.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: NASA Astronaut Jessica Meir Shares Dazzling Moonlit Earth View From Space
news.excerpt: The Crew-12 commander posted the "Milky Way with a Moonlit Earth" clip on X days before her return from the International Space Station, calling it motivation for NASA's Artemis program.
news.image_caption: A view of Earth from orbit with the International Space Station solar arrays visible against a star-filled sky. NASA astronaut Jessica Meir posted a video of a moonlit Earth from space during her Crew-12 mission this week.
news.nri_angle: Moments like Meir's moonlit video travel fast across the Indian diaspora, where Indian-origin astronauts such as Sunita Williams have turned NASA missions into shared community events.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Amritsar Police Bust Pakistan-Linked Terror Module, Seize AK-47 and Grenades
news.excerpt: Amritsar Rural Police arrested 28-year-old truck driver Navjot Singh and recovered an AK-47 rifle, two hand grenades and nine live cartridges allegedly pushed across the border by drone.
news.image_caption: Punjab Police officers address the media in Amritsar after announcing the bust of a cross-border terror module on Sunday. Police recovered an AK-47 rifle, two hand grenades and ammunition allegedly pushed into India by drones.
news.nri_angle: The large Punjabi diaspora in Canada, the US and the UK closely tracks border-security developments, and many families still live in the Tarn Taran-Amritsar belt where the module was operating.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Russian Drone Strikes Kyiv Bridge as Germany's Merz Arrives to Sirens
news.excerpt: Merz landed in Kyiv to pledge €1 billion in military aid and a joint drone-production deal as Russia's defence ministry said it would intensify strikes on Ukrainian military-industrial targets.
news.image_caption: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz is greeted at a Kyiv railway station on Sunday during his visit to Ukraine. His arrival coincided with a Russian drone strike on the city’s Pivnichnyi Bridge, which injured two people.
news.nri_angle: Germany hosts Europe's largest Ukrainian refugee population and a large Indian diaspora, both watching how the new aid package and energy-repair commitments affect Berlin's defence spending and winter energy costs.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Jaishankar Says India Has Gone 'Beyond Advocacy' in Russia-Ukraine Conflict
news.excerpt: At the Munich Leaders Meeting, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar said New Delhi is now holding direct talks with both Moscow and Kyiv on Black Sea shipping, grain and energy exports, and 'non-attack possibilities'.
news.image_caption: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, who said India has gone 'beyond advocacy' in the Russia-Ukraine conflict at the Munich Leaders Meeting.
news.nri_angle: India's deeper diplomatic engagement signals New Delhi's confidence in its standing with both Moscow and Kyiv — and its ability to protect the energy and trade interests that affect Indian households and diaspora businesses.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Russian Drones Destroy Indian-Run Kusum Pharma Plant in Ukraine, One Killed
news.excerpt: The main structure of the Kusum Group's Sumy facility was largely destroyed in Sunday's strike, which killed one worker and injured several others. The company puts its losses at at least ₹400 crore.
news.image_caption: A plume of dark smoke rises from an industrial building after a drone strike. The aftermath of the Russian drone attack that largely destroyed the Kusum Group’s pharmaceutical plant in Sumy, Ukraine, killed one worker and injured several others.
news.nri_angle: An Indian-run pharmaceutical company that grew from exporting Indian medicines to Ukraine into a major local manufacturer has lost its flagship Ukrainian plant to the war, putting hundreds of Ukrainian jobs and an Indian business success story at risk.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: LGBTQ Influencer Mad Sandhu Shot Dead in Amritsar, Sparking Punjab Law-and-Order Row
news.excerpt: Mad Sandhu, a makeup artist with 2.26 lakh Instagram followers, was gunned down by two motorcycle-borne men on Saturday evening; the BJP and Congress blamed the AAP government's law-and-order record as police said they had leads.
news.image_caption: Makeup artist and LGBTQ influencer Mad Sandhu in a photo from his Instagram account. Sandhu, who had about 2.26 lakh followers, was shot dead in Amritsar on October 3, 2026.
news.nri_angle: Punjab's large overseas diaspora follows law-and-order developments closely given family ties and safety concerns back home; the killing also touches diaspora conversations on LGBTQ visibility and safety in Punjabi society.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Five Indian-Origin Men Face Extortion, Weapons and Drug Charges in BC Task-Force Sweep
news.excerpt: Langley RCMP's 16-month Project E_PURSUANCE ended with arrests, firearms and drug seizures — and more charges are expected across BC and Alberta.
news.nri_angle: The extortion wave gripping BC's South Asian business community has become one of the top diaspora safety issues in Canada; these arrests are the biggest scalp yet for the province's anti-extortion task force, and victims coming forward made it possible.

nri-world.title: San Jose Seventh-Grader Boosts Air-to-Water Output 117%, Reaches National STEM Final
nri-world.excerpt: Ankith Burki built an atmospheric water generator from scratch, found that low-frequency sound waves dramatically increased its water collection, and earned a finalist spot in the 2026 Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge.
nri-world.image_caption: San Jose seventh-grader Ankith Burki. His air-to-water prototype reached the national final of the 2026 Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge.
nri-world.nri_angle: For Indian-American families, Burki's achievement shows diaspora youth using STEM to tackle water scarcity — a problem with deep relevance to India, where water stress affects hundreds of millions.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: GIFT City Emerges as NRI Magnet With $54 Billion Banking Push
nri-world.excerpt: Nearly 500 wealthy Indians used the FCNR(B) facility through the GIFT IFSC for the first time — many discovering the financial centre for the first time — and regulators are moving to keep them with bigger investments.
nri-world.image_caption: K Rajaraman, chairman of the International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA), the unified regulator of GIFT City. Rajaraman said nearly 500 high-net-worth NRIs used the FCNR(B) facility through the GIFT IFSC for the first time.
nri-world.nri_angle: GIFT City is built for how NRIs handle money: dollar-denominated investing with no INR conversion, no transaction taxes and unrestricted repatriation through a single Indian-regulated financial centre.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Indian American Geneticist Pradeep Natarajan to Receive AHA's 2026 Population Research Prize
nri-world.excerpt: The Harvard and Mass General physician-scientist, who joined Amgen in August to lead human genetics, will be honored on Nov. 8 in Chicago for transforming how genetics and big population studies prevent heart disease.
nri-world.image_caption: Dr. Pradeep Natarajan, the Harvard Medical School and Massachusetts General Hospital cardiovascular geneticist. He will receive the American Heart Association’s 2026 Population Research Prize on Nov. 8 in Chicago.
nri-world.nri_angle: Dr. Pradeep Natarajan's AHA prize is a milestone for Indian Americans in medical research — and his polygenic heart-risk work speaks directly to South Asians, who face among the highest cardiovascular risk of any group.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Two Teenagers Jailed 10 Years for Petrol Arson Attack on Indian Restaurant in London
nri-world.excerpt: The Old Bailey heard the August 2025 attack on Indian Aroma in Gants Hill was a 'sophisticated and professional operation' that left a couple in their 20s with life-changing burns.
nri-world.nri_angle: Indian restaurants are community anchors across the UK; an attack of this severity on a family-run eatery resonates with the million-plus Indian diaspora in Britain and its business owners.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Telangana Woman Killed in Missouri Truck Crash; Family Seeks Help to Bring Body Home
nri-world.excerpt: Daram Supriya, 31, from Mahabubabad district, died after a speeding truck hit her car in Missouri; the family has appealed for help bringing her body home for final rites.
nri-world.image_caption: Daram Supriya, 31, from Maripeda in Telangana's Mahabubabad district, in a photo published by IndiaToday with its report on the crash. She died after the car she was traveling in was struck from behind by a speeding truck in Missouri on October 4, 2026.
nri-world.nri_angle: A Telugu worker's death in Missouri leaves her Mahabubabad family navigating the painful, slow process of repatriating her body — a recurring ordeal for the Indian diaspora.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Bangladesh Presses India to Speed Up Sheikh Hasina Extradition
nri-world.excerpt: Indian High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi said New Delhi cannot commit to a timeline, stressing that the extradition request is being examined through an established legal process under the bilateral treaty.
nri-world.image_caption: Sheikh Hasina, Bangladeshs former prime minister, speaks at an event with the Bangladeshi flag behind her. Dhaka has asked India to expedite her extradition so she can face charges at home.
nri-world.nri_angle: The extradition standoff shapes India-Bangladesh relations, which touch the millions of people with family, business, and cultural ties across the border, as well as the flow of trade and travel between the two countries.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: UK's Oldest Indian Restaurant Accuses Crown Estate of Cultural Ignorance in Eviction Row
nri-world.excerpt: Veeraswamy, serving diners on London's Regent Street since 1926, is fighting the Crown Estate's refusal to renew its lease — a dispute whose court hearing has now been delayed until at least late autumn.
nri-world.image_caption: A doorman in Veeraswamy uniform stands outside the restaurant’s facade at Victory House on Regent Street. The century-old restaurant is fighting the Crown Estate’s refusal to renew its lease, a dispute whose court hearing has been delayed until at least late autumn 2026.
nri-world.nri_angle: A century-old Indian institution on London's Regent Street is fighting to survive against its royal landlord, making the case that Indian heritage in Britain deserves protection from commercial redevelopment.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Ranveer Singh Becomes Ray-Ban's First Brand Ambassador in India
nri-world.excerpt: The Bollywood star will front Ray-Ban and Ray-Ban Meta in India, headlining the 'Frame Your True Self' campaign as Meta's Gen 3 smart glasses go on sale starting at ₹44,300.
nri-world.image_caption: Ranveer Singh wears round Ray-Ban sunglasses and a red leather jacket in a campaign portrait. Ray-Ban named him its first brand ambassador in India on October 1, 2026.
nri-world.nri_angle: An Indian film star fronting a global brand's AI-eyewear push in India gives the diaspora a cultural foothold in a technology launch that will shape how wearables are received across South Asia.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India-Born Scientist Shankar Balasubramanian Wins 2026 Wolf Chemistry Prize
nri-world.excerpt: The Cambridge chemist shares the award with David Klenerman and Pascal Mayer for the DNA-sequencing technology that cut the cost of reading a human genome from over $1 billion to about $1,000.
nri-world.image_caption: Shankar Balasubramanian, a chemistry professor at the University of Cambridge, in a university portrait. He shared the 2026 Wolf Prize in Chemistry for the DNA-sequencing technology behind Solexa/Illumina.
nri-world.image_credit: Nathan Pitt / University of Cambridge via hayadan.com
nri-world.nri_angle: An India-born chemist winning the Wolf Prize — one year after an Indian American physicist won it — marks a second straight year of Indian-diaspora laureates at one of science's top honors.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: September's Global Immigration Shifts: What Changed for Visa Seekers Worldwide
immigration.excerpt: From Australia's new skilled-visa priority rules to Japan's twentyfold permanent residence fee hike and a UK settlement overhaul on the horizon, September brought rule changes that directly affect Indian migrants.
immigration.image_caption: WR Immigration's September 2026 global immigration recap graphic. The recap covers rule changes in Canada, Australia, the United Kingdom, Japan, Saudi Arabia, New Zealand, and Thailand.
immigration.nri_angle: Australia's onshore-first processing favors Indian students and graduates already in the country, while the UK's coming earned-settlement overhaul could reshape ILR eligibility for thousands of Indians nearing five years of residence.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: Montana Governor Lands in India to Rescue Lentil Exports Amid MAGA Backlash
immigration.excerpt: Governor Greg Gianforte is leading a 30-member delegation to India and Sri Lanka to rebuild the state's collapsed pulse trade, even as anti-India voices in his own party attack the trip.
immigration.nri_angle: The trip exposes a paradox for Indian Americans: anti-India voices demand the governor's impeachment while Montana's farm economy and universities actively court Indian consumers, students, and research ties.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: Mother of US Green Card Holder Denied Visitor Visa: 214(b) Rules and Interview Tips
immigration.excerpt: A Green Card holder's mother was refused a B1/B2 visitor visa within minutes at the Mumbai consulate despite showing savings, property and investments. Reddit users - and the 214(b) rule itself - say it was never about money at all.
immigration.image_caption: The US Embassy in New Delhi. The mother of a US green card holder was denied a visitor visa under Section 214(b).
immigration.nri_angle: Green Card holders and US citizens inviting parents over must build the case around the parent's roots in India - steady income, property, a short specific itinerary - because a 214(b) denial has no appeal, only a stronger reapplication.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: DACA and TPS Holders Face Tougher Travel Rules After Immigration Appeals Board Ruling
immigration.excerpt: The August decision overturns a 12-year-old rule — advance parole trips can now trigger three- or 10-year bars on reentry to the United States.
immigration.image_caption: Supporters at a DACA rally. A Board of Immigration Appeals ruling means DACA and TPS holders who leave the US could trigger reentry bars.
immigration.nri_angle: Indian DACA recipients and adjustment-of-status applicants lose a once-safe travel option, raising the stakes of every family visit home.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: Russia to Take 70,000 Indian Skilled Workers This Year, Jaishankar Tells Parliament Panel
immigration.excerpt: The external affairs minister's briefing covered trade, energy and Ukraine diplomacy — plus India's push to bring home citizens recruited into Russia's military.
immigration.image_caption: S. Jaishankar, India's External Affairs Minister, who told Parliament that Russia will take 70,000 Indian skilled workers this year.
immigration.nri_angle: The 70,000-worker commitment opens a major new overseas employment channel for Indians, alongside the government's effort to repatriate those fraudulently recruited into Russia's military.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: Five Visa Application Mistakes First-Time Travelers Must Avoid
immigration.excerpt: Most visa refusals for first-time travelers come down to avoidable errors — mismatched documents, weak financial proof, vague itineraries, passport validity and dishonest disclosures. Here's how to get each one right.
immigration.image_caption: An Indian passport — documentation errors are the top driver of visa rejections for first-time travellers
immigration.nri_angle: First-time Indian travelers most often need visas for the diaspora's core routes — the US, UK, Canada and the Gulf — so these documentation rules are the practical gateway to visiting family abroad.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

immigration.title: India Exempt From $20,000 US Visa Bond Rule as 50 Countries Listed
immigration.excerpt: The US State Department has finalized a permanent visa-bond program for B1/B2 applicants from 50 countries, with bonds of $10,000 to $20,000 set at consular officers' discretion. Indian passport holders are not on the list.
immigration.image_caption: A woman holding an Indian passport speaks with a consular officer at a US visa application window. Indian passport holders are exempt from the new US visa-bond requirement, which covers B1/B2 applicants from 50 listed countries.
immigration.nri_angle: Indian passport holders are exempt, but the diaspora should track the list because it covers neighboring countries many Indian-American families receive relatives from.
immigration.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Schneider Electric to Buy PTC for $22.6 Billion in Its Biggest Deal Ever
markets-finance.excerpt: The $205-a-share all-cash offer, a 42.3% premium, sent PTC shares up nearly 34% on Monday. Schneider's stock fell about 10% in Paris as investors weighed the price and the up-to-EUR-23-billion financing plan.
markets-finance.image_caption: Schneider Electric’s headquarters. The French engineering group agreed to acquire US industrial software company PTC for $22.6 billion in cash.
markets-finance.nri_angle: No direct impact for most readers, but the deal is another major bet on data-centre and industrial-AI infrastructure, a sector employing a large Indian tech workforce in the US and Europe.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: HDFC Bank Taps ICICI's Anup Bagchi as CEO With Stock Down 27% in 2026
markets-finance.excerpt: RBI approved Anup Bagchi's appointment as MD and CEO for a three-year term from October 27, 2026, ending months of succession uncertainty. Jefferies reaffirmed HDFC Bank as its top Indian pick with a Rs 880 target, even as the stock sits 27% below its 2025 close.
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRIs holding HDB ADRs or Indian bank ETFs have absorbed a 27% slide in 2026; an external CEO with a retail-franchise track record offers a reset narrative, though execution risk is real.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Tops Global SIP Returns: 74% of 5-Year Periods Beat 8% Mark
markets-finance.excerpt: DSP Asset Managers' 30-year, 16-country study found India the most rewarding market for systematic investors — though recent five-year Nifty SIP returns of ~4.5% show the average hides deep swings.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai. Indian SIP investors saw strong five-year returns.
markets-finance.nri_angle: For NRIs comparing India with other markets, India's SIP edge in the DSP data is nominal — higher inflation and currency moves eat into it — while SPIVA data showing 84% of large-cap funds trailing benchmarks argues for low-cost index SIPs over active fund-picking.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: US Student Loan Defaults Hit $234 Billion — and Collections May Restart
markets-finance.excerpt: Federal data through June 30 shows 9.3 million borrowers in default — up from 7.7 million six months earlier — as the Trump administration keeps involuntary collections paused while it stands up a new support system.
markets-finance.image_caption: A chart of US consumer and government debt, including student loans. (Wikimedia Commons)
markets-finance.nri_angle: Indian students and recent graduates financing US degrees through federal loans face the same garnishment and credit consequences as any borrower — and the new repayment plans launched in July matter to anyone holding F-1 OPT-era debt.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Jio IPO Likely by October-End at $143-146 Billion Valuation
markets-finance.excerpt: Banking sources say Jio Platforms' estimated $3.8 billion public offering — potentially India's largest IPO — could list by month-end, with an anchor round before Dussehra and final SEBI filings in the week starting October 12.
markets-finance.nri_angle: At $143-146 billion the valuation is legible to diaspora investors in global terms; NRIs with demat accounts can apply for Indian IPOs on the same terms as residents.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Within Striking Distance of 8% Growth, Says PMO's Shaktikanta Das
markets-finance.excerpt: The former RBI governor credited a decade of reforms — GST, banking clean-up, inflation targeting, digital payments — for 7.8% June-quarter growth, and named AI the next productivity frontier.
markets-finance.image_caption: Shaktikanta Das, principal secretary to the prime minister and former RBI governor, at the Kautilya Economic Conclave in New Delhi
markets-finance.nri_angle: The domestic-demand growth story underpins the NRI investment case — steady remittances, services surplus and deepening capital markets keep the macro backdrop for diaspora portfolios supportive.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Why Diesel Costs More Than Gasoline — and When the Flip Happened
markets-finance.excerpt: National diesel is averaging $6.38 a gallon, nearly $2 above gasoline. Three structural reasons — demand, cleaner-fuel rules and taxes — plus the Iran war's supply shock explain the gap.
markets-finance.image_caption: Diesel fuel pump at a gas station. Diesel averaged .38 a gallon nationally, holding above gasoline since September 2004
markets-finance.nri_angle: India's early-2000s motorizing boom was one of the demand drivers that helped flip diesel's price against gasoline; today the $6.38 average hits US consumers broadly, including Indian-American families in trucking and logistics.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Warsh's 'Dose of Accommodation' Remark Has Wall Street Bracing for More Fed Rate Hikes
markets-finance.excerpt: The Fed chairman's deliberate phrasing after September's rate hike — the first in three years — has traders, banks and economists debating how many more increases are coming.
markets-finance.nri_angle: U.S.-based Indian diaspora homebuyers and borrowers face mortgage rates tied to the 10-year Treasury's 19-year high as the Fed signals more hikes.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Weathered Global Turbulence With Fundamentals Intact, Sitharaman Tells Economists
markets-finance.excerpt: Citing 7.8% Q1 growth, 4.82% August inflation and $766 billion in forex reserves, the finance minister told the Kautilya Economic Conclave that a decade of reforms built India's shock-absorbing capacity.
markets-finance.image_caption: Nirmala Sitharaman, India's Union Finance Minister, speaks at an event. She said India had navigated four years of global shocks with its economic fundamentals intact and strengthening.
markets-finance.nri_angle: The macro picture — 7.8% growth, contained inflation, thick forex buffers — is the backdrop behind record diaspora interest in Indian equities and GIFT City instruments.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: FPIs Turn Net Sellers, Pull ₹35,860 Crore From Indian Equities in September
markets-finance.excerpt: A two-month buying streak ended as elevated US bond yields, high crude prices and a rotation into AI-led markets pushed foreign investors to the exits, putting 2026 on track for record annual outflows.
markets-finance.nri_angle: For India-focused investors in the US and globally, the record pace of foreign withdrawals shows global capital is pricing Indian equities against high US yields and elevated valuations — a re-rating, not a dismissal, of the India growth story.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: With Asian Games Gold Secured, India Hockey Eyes Los Angeles 2028
sports.excerpt: India's men defended their Asian Games hockey title with a 5-1 win over Malaysia, the women ended a 44-year wait against China, and both squads have booked direct tickets to LA 2028.
sports.image_caption: India's men's hockey team celebrates with gold medals behind an LA 2028 'Qualified' banner. The 5-1 win over Malaysia in the Asian Games final was India's first successful title defence and booked a direct Olympic berth.
sports.nri_angle: LA 2028 lets Indian-Americans watch India chase Olympic hockey gold on home soil for the first time, with both the men's and women's teams qualified directly.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Archery Premier League Returns to Hyderabad as Asian Games Stars Turn Rivals
sports.excerpt: Less than a week after India won nine Asian Games archery medals, the stars trade national jerseys for franchise rivalries in the Archery Premier League's second season, running October 8–18 in Hyderabad.
sports.image_caption: The Archery Premier League logo. Season 2 of the franchise archery league begins in Hyderabad on October 8, with 48 archers across six teams competing over 11 days.
sports.nri_angle: The APL gives Indian fans abroad a new way to follow archery — and an early look at the archers India will field at Los Angeles 2028, which many in the US diaspora will attend.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Hardik Pandya Trade Back on Table as Franchise Makes Fresh Inquiry
sports.excerpt: Cricbuzz reports renewed franchise interest in the Mumbai Indians captain, with the next three to four weeks likely decisive — but MI publicly insists no trade talks are on until its post-season review is done.
sports.image_caption: Hardik Pandya in a Mumbai Indians training kit. The 32-year-old all-rounder’s IPL future is the subject of renewed trade speculation ahead of the November 15 retention deadline.
sports.nri_angle: A Pandya trade would redraw IPL loyalties for the diaspora's watch-party and fantasy-league audience overnight — the debate among Indian-origin fans is already about fit, not money.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Diego Forlan Warns Uruguay: Be Careful Against India's Young Talent
sports.excerpt: Ahead of Tuesday's historic India-Uruguay friendly in Kolkata, the 2010 World Cup Golden Ball winner says the Blue Tigers have "a lot of young footballing talent" — but need a stronger league and academies to develop them.
sports.image_caption: Diego Forlán, head coach of Uruguay, at the pre-match press conference in Kolkata. He is in India ahead of Uruguay’s historic friendly against the Blue Tigers at Salt Lake Stadium on Tuesday.
sports.nri_angle: Forlan's insider verdict — talent is abundant, pathways are not — speaks directly to diaspora football families weighing where a young player's serious career can be built.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Jyothi Surekha Gets Hero's Welcome After Archery Gold With Record-Equaling Score
sports.excerpt: India's women's compound team beat China 238-234 in the Asian Games final at Aichi-Nagoya, matching a 12-year-old world record — the 30-year-old veteran's fourth Asiad gold.
sports.image_caption: Members of India's women's compound archery team — Jyothi Surekha Vennam, Chikitha Taniparthi and Prithika Pradeep — stand on the podium with their gold medals at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games. The trio beat China 238-234 in the final, matching the world record set by South Korea in 2014.
sports.nri_angle: A world-record-equaling Asian Games gold in a sport India quietly dominates — the kind of result that travels fast across diaspora group chats, from a veteran who has also won on American soil.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Shreyas Iyer Backs Vaibhav Sooryavanshi: 'When His Time Comes, He'll Dominate Indian Cricket'
sports.excerpt: India's T20I captain praised the 15-year-old's quiet dressing-room presence and destructive batting, predicting Vaibhav Sooryavanshi will dominate Indian cricket once his opportunity arrives.
sports.image_caption: Shreyas Iyer (left) and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi in India training kit. Iyer said the 15-year-old will dominate Indian cricket when his time comes.
sports.nri_angle: For the Indian diaspora, Sooryavanshi's rise is a unifying story — a 15-year-old rewriting record books in India blue, with the October 6–17 West Indies T20I series the next appointment viewing for overseas fans.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Bhuvneshwar Kumar to Captain India at Hong Kong Sixes 2026
sports.excerpt: The veteran pacer will lead an IPL-heavy Indian seven at the October 30–November 1 six-a-side tournament in Hong Kong, with Krunal Pandya, Rahul Tewatia and T. Natarajan among the squad.
sports.image_caption: The official Team India squad graphic for the Hong Kong Sixes 2026, with captain Bhuvneshwar Kumar joined by Krunal Pandya, Shashank Singh, Nitish Rana, T. Natarajan, Rahul Tewatia and Rahul Tripathi. Kumar will lead the seven-member IPL-heavy side at the October 30 to November 1 tournament.
sports.nri_angle: For diaspora cricket fans, India's IPL-heavy squad playing the rapid six-a-side format is a prime-time-friendly spectacle — a rare chance to see established stars adapt their games outside conventional T20.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Asian Games Cricket Champions Return Home After Defending Gold Against Pakistan
sports.excerpt: India's men landed in Delhi and Hyderabad to a warm welcome a day after head coach VVS Laxman hailed the 19-run win over Pakistan as a matter of great pride for Indian cricket.
sports.image_caption: VVS Laxman speaks to reporters after arriving in India. The head coach praised the men's squad after it defended the Asian Games T20 gold with a 19-run win over Pakistan.
sports.nri_angle: The India-Pakistan final drew record viewership among the diaspora, and the squad's homecoming caps a Games where Indian athletes delivered 85 medals.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India Beat Pakistan by 19 Runs to Defend Asian Games Cricket Gold
sports.excerpt: Abhishek Sharma's 61 and Tilak Varma's unbeaten 51 powered India to 211/6 before the spinners held off Hasan Nawaz's 96 in a 19-run final win at Nisshin.
sports.image_caption: India's cricket team in action. India beat Pakistan by 19 runs to defend the Asian Games men's cricket gold medal.
sports.nri_angle: The final froze two time zones at once — morning in the US, evening in India — with diaspora WhatsApp groups as commentary boxes; the win keeps India on track for LA 2028, where the diaspora will be among the loudest in the stands.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India-Pakistan Cricket Final and Hockey Semi-Final Set Asian Games Viewership Records
sports.excerpt: The Olympic Council of Asia said Sunday that the two India-Pakistan clashes at Aichi-Nagoya drew the biggest broadcast audience in Asian Games history — and India won both matches before taking gold in each sport.
sports.image_caption: Two Indian hockey players celebrate during a match at the FIH Hockey World Cup in 2026. India beat Pakistan 4-3 in the Asian Games hockey semifinal at Aichi-Nagoya, one of two India-Pakistan clashes the Olympic Council of Asia called the most-viewed in the event’s history.
sports.nri_angle: Indian diaspora audiences from New Jersey to Dubai form a large share of the global viewership for India-Pakistan fixtures, making this weekend's double-header and record audience a shared cultural moment.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: 'Appan Chale Punjab Medal Lai Ke': Baljeet Kaur's Video Goes Viral After Hockey Gold
sports.excerpt: The India hockey star's Punjabi message to fans after the team's 1-0 Asian Games final win over China became an internet favourite.
sports.image_caption: Indian hockey defender Baljeet Kaur, whose celebratory video went viral after India's Asian Games gold
sports.nri_angle: A Punjabi hockey star's viral video in her mother tongue turned India's Asian Games gold into a shared celebration for Punjabi communities worldwide.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India Seals Fourth at Asian Games With 85 Medals After Late Gold Rush
sports.excerpt: India finished fourth at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Saturday, winning 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals after a late two-day surge that delivered historic firsts in archery and golf.
sports.image_caption: The medal standings graphic from the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026 shows India in fourth place with 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals. India finished ahead of fifth-placed Uzbekistan after a late gold rush across the final two days of competition.
sports.nri_angle: Nagoya's Indian community watched a 48-hour gold rush carry India from outside the top 10 to fourth, with historic firsts in women's archery and golf and multiple LA 2028 Olympic berths booked.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: OpenAI to Add Invisible Text Watermarks to ChatGPT and Codex in the EU
technology.excerpt: OpenAI's textGrain system subtly shapes word choices so detectors can spot AI-generated text, complying with the EU AI Act. API developers worldwide can opt in; the detector stays limited to approved researchers.
technology.image_caption: The ChatGPT app icon on a smartphone. OpenAI said it will add an invisible statistical watermark to eligible ChatGPT and Codex text in the European Union over the coming weeks.
technology.nri_angle: No change for users outside the EU — watermarking is EU-only and opt-in on the API — but educators, employers and compliance teams should know these marks are invisible, fragile and often absent.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: First Microblazar Found in Milky Way: Black Hole Jet Aimed at Earth
technology.excerpt: IRAS 18293−0941, a stellar-mass black hole 12,000 light-years away firing plasma at 75% light speed toward Earth, is the first confirmed microblazar — and a 100-times-more-powerful natural accelerator than the LHC.
technology.image_caption: Artist impression of microblazar IRAS 18293−0941, with one jet aimed almost at Earth (left) and the other striking a molecular cloud. The system, 12,000 light-years away, is the first confirmed microblazar in the Milky Way. Illustration: B. Marcote (JIVE/ASTRON).
technology.nri_angle: India's radio astronomers regularly join multi-observatory campaigns like this one, and the GMRT near Pune shares survey skies with MeerKAT, whose images confirmed the microblazar's counter-jet hotspot.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India Demonstrates First Free-Space Quantum Link Over 5.56 km of Air
technology.excerpt: QNu Labs' overnight trial between BISAG-N and IIT Gandhinagar transmitted secure encryption keys through open air with an error rate below 5%, laying the groundwork for satellite-based quantum communication.
technology.image_caption: Laboratory equipment for quantum key distribution research, including server racks, fibre-optic spools and monitoring displays. QNu Labs demonstrated Indias first free-space QKD link over 5.56 km of open air between BISAG-N and IIT Gandhinagar on the night of Sept. 27-28.
technology.nri_angle: The quantum-encrypted systems that will eventually secure UPI payments and NRI remittances are being tested and owned domestically; the diaspora's financial links to India will rest on this indigenous stack.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Four Indian Space Startups Ride SpaceX's Transporter-18 to Orbit
technology.excerpt: TakeMe2Space's MOI-1A, Dhruva Space's LEAP-2, SatLeo's TAPAS-1 and EON's MIRA imaging system all reached orbit aboard the October 1 rideshare from Vandenberg.
technology.image_caption: A SpaceX Falcon 9 lifts off on a Transporter rideshare mission. Four Indian space startups flew on the Transporter-18 mission.
technology.nri_angle: Indian space startups are selling heavily abroad — 80 percent of TakeMe2Space's customers are outside India, and French firm Sodern flew on Dhruva's platform — making the sector one of India's strongest diaspora-relevant tech exports.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Indian Startups Raised $233 Million Last Week as Simple Energy's $180M Round Dominated
technology.excerpt: Sixteen Indian startups raised $233.6 million in the week of Sept 28–Oct 2, per Inc42's tracker — but Simple Energy's $180 million Series C alone made up three-quarters of it.
technology.image_caption: A stock illustration of a tablet displaying startup-themed doodles. Indian startups raised $233.6 million across 16 deals in the week of September 28–October 2, 2026, according to Inc42's weekly tracker.
technology.nri_angle: For diaspora investors tracking India's startup ecosystem, growth-stage capital is flowing again — led by cleantech and EV — while early-stage founders face a tougher raise.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Google Pauses Open-Source Bug Bounty Over Flood of AI-Generated 'Slop' Reports
technology.excerpt: Google stopped accepting new product vulnerability reports to its OSS VRP on October 1, saying a "significant rise in automated submissions" — mostly AI-generated and invalid — had overwhelmed maintainers.
technology.image_caption: The Googleplex in Mountain View. Google has paused its open-source bug bounty after a flood of AI-generated low-quality reports.
technology.nri_angle: India is one of the largest sources of independent security researchers; the freeze raises the bar for them — volume submissions are out, demonstrably real high-impact flaws are the only paying path left.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Android 17 QPR3 Beta 1 Arrives With 20-Plus Pixel Fixes
technology.excerpt: Google's first QPR3 beta targets Pixel 6a and newer, drops the Pixel 6 and 6 Pro, and carries early code pointing to gamepad cursor control and phone-to-device unlock.
technology.nri_angle: The fixed eSIM self-disable bug is a genuine win for readers who toggle between a US line and a local eSIM while traveling; the beta's feature hints matter most to Pixel's enthusiast base, which includes many in the diaspora.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Global Factory Output Hits Four-Year High as AI Demand Lifts Manufacturing PMIs Worldwide
technology.excerpt: September PMI data shows the broadest industrial expansion since early 2022, led by euro zone factories and Asia's chip-exporting economies.
technology.image_caption: A semiconductor fabrication plant. Global factory output hit a four-year high as AI demand lifted manufacturing
technology.nri_angle: The AI-driven factory expansion touches India's semiconductor and manufacturing ambitions as global chip and equipment demand accelerates.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Infosys Extends ABN AMRO Tie-Up to Push Enterprise-Wide AI in Dutch Banking
technology.excerpt: The renewal brings Infosys Topaz's generative and agentic AI into ABN AMRO's core systems — announced a day after the stock hit a 52-week low.
technology.image_caption: The Infosys logo on a company sign. Infosys extended its strategic collaboration with ABN AMRO on September 30 to simplify the Dutch bank’s IT landscape and push enterprise-wide AI adoption.
technology.nri_angle: India's IT flagship is moving from AI pilots to enterprise-wide AI inside a major European bank even as the market punishes the stock (down 38% YTD) — a tension that defines the careers of millions of Indian tech professionals.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: OpenAI Takes on Microsoft With ChatGPT's Own Office Suite at DevDay
technology.excerpt: At DevDay in San Francisco, OpenAI unveiled Space, Pages, and collaborative slides — workplace tools that put the ChatGPT maker in direct competition with Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace.
technology.image_caption: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. The company announced Space, Pages and collaborative slides inside ChatGPT at DevDay in San Francisco.
technology.nri_angle: For the large Indian diaspora workforce in American tech, the change is practical: documents and decks where distributed teams collaborate are becoming the place where AI agents operate.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Wipro Merges VLSI Design Subsidiary Into IT Services Arm
technology.excerpt: Wipro has merged its US chip-design subsidiary, formerly Eximius Design, into its IT services entity effective October 1, 2026, continuing its drive to simplify the group structure. There is no cash consideration and no change in shareholding.
technology.image_caption: Wipro has merged its VLSI design subsidiary Wipro VLSI Design Services into Wipro IT Services
technology.nri_angle: Wipro is NYSE-listed and widely held by Indian-American investors, and the absorbed unit traces back to a Silicon Valley semiconductor firm founded by an Indian immigrant.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Microsoft Expands Circular Centers to Give Retired Azure Servers New Life
technology.excerpt: Eight Circular Centers across three continents now securely decommission retired Azure hardware, hitting a 92% reuse and recycling rate as the AI buildout accelerates.
technology.image_caption: A data center aisle of server racks, in a Microsoft graphic about the Azure hardware lifecycle. Circular Centers process decommissioned servers and components from Microsoft's global fleet, reaching a 92% reuse and recycling rate last year.
technology.nri_angle: Indian cloud-infrastructure engineers staff much of the global Azure data-center workforce, and Indian enterprises on Azure gain verifiable hardware-reuse metrics for ESG reporting.

carousel.title: OpenAI to Add Invisible Text Watermarks to ChatGPT and Codex in the EU
carousel.excerpt: OpenAI's textGrain system subtly shapes word choices so detectors can spot AI-generated text, complying with the EU AI Act. API developers worldwide can opt in; the detector stays limited to approved researchers.
carousel.image_caption: The ChatGPT app icon on a smartphone. OpenAI said it will add an invisible statistical watermark to eligible ChatGPT and Codex text in the European Union over the coming weeks.
carousel.nri_angle: No change for users outside the EU — watermarking is EU-only and opt-in on the API — but educators, employers and compliance teams should know these marks are invisible, fragile and often absent.

carousel.title: Schneider Electric to Buy PTC for $22.6 Billion in Its Biggest Deal Ever
carousel.excerpt: The $205-a-share all-cash offer, a 42.3% premium, sent PTC shares up nearly 34% on Monday. Schneider's stock fell about 10% in Paris as investors weighed the price and the up-to-EUR-23-billion financing plan.
carousel.image_caption: Schneider Electric’s headquarters. The French engineering group agreed to acquire US industrial software company PTC for $22.6 billion in cash.
carousel.nri_angle: No direct impact for most readers, but the deal is another major bet on data-centre and industrial-AI infrastructure, a sector employing a large Indian tech workforce in the US and Europe.
